result.description:
Location: Balaklava, SA, 5461
Full-Time: Immediate start
Reports to: Aged Care Facility Manager
Job Title: Personal Care Assistant
Salary range: $79,500 - $85,000 - depending on skills level and work experience + superannuation.
Job Closure date: 30 days

About the Role
On behalf of our client, an independent, not-for-profit aged care provider known as “the heart of country care,” we are seeking a compassionate Personal Care Assistant. Our client proudly supports older South Australians in regional communities with safe, caring, and inclusive living environments across residential aged care and retirement living. They are passionate about developing respectful, warm, and genuine relationships where everyone is valued and everyone matters. We are looking for a Personal Care Assistant who will deliver quality care through mutual respect in a warm, caring country environment, empowering residents to make choices about their life, support, and care.

Key Duties (paraphrased & detailed)
Resident-Centred Personal Care & Support
• Deliver high-quality personal care including gentle assistance with bathing, showering, dressing, grooming, toileting, and mobility support (transfers, walking), always following each resident’s individual care plan.
• Promote independence and dignity by encouraging residents to participate in daily activities at their comfort level, supporting them to maintain skills and choice.
• Provide emotional support and genuine companionship, engaging residents in meaningful conversations, reminiscence activities, and recreational pursuits that combat loneliness.

Specialised Care & Health Monitoring
• Assist with specialised care needs including dementia support (using calm, reassuring communication), palliative care (comfort-focused assistance), and behavioural interventions under the guidance of registered nurses.
• Observe and report any changes in residents’ physical or emotional condition (e.g., skin integrity, mood swings, appetite loss) to senior staff in a timely manner.
• Accurately document care provided and contributed to care plan reviews, ensuring resident needs are continuously met and their preferences respected.

Wellness Programs & Therapy Support
• Support therapy and wellness programs by assisting with gentle exercises (range of motion, seated stretching), cognitive stimulation activities (puzzles, memory games), and social outings within the local community.
• Encourage resident participation in group activities that foster connection and engagement, aligned with the “heart of country care” ethos.

Safety, Compliance & Environmental Care
• Adhere strictly to infection control protocols (hand hygiene, PPE use), workplace health & safety policies, and Aged Care Quality Standards to protect vulnerable residents.
• Maintain a clean, hazard-free environment, ensuring resident rooms, communal areas, and bathrooms meet hygiene standards and are free from trip risks.
• Participate in emergency response procedures including fire drills, evacuation support, and basic first aid interventions when required (certification preferred).

Team Collaboration, Communication & Continuous Improvement
• Build trusting relationships with residents’ families, providing empathetic updates on care and addressing concerns with professionalism and warmth.
• Work closely with nurses, allied health professionals (physiotherapists, OTs), and other care staff to ensure a holistic, person-centred approach to resident wellbeing.
• Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives by sharing feedback, participating in staff meetings, attending training sessions, and identifying self-education needs.

Skills & Experience Required
• Certificate III in Aged Care, Individual Support, or equivalent qualification.
• Minimum 1-year full-time experience in a similar role (residential aged care preferred).
• NDIS Worker Screening Clearance (issued within last 5 years) – preferable.
• Up-to-date flu vaccination and full COVID-19 immunisation.
• Satisfactory police check with no disclosures; valid driver’s licence and own reliable transportation.
• Strong teamwork skills, compassionate communication, and a genuine commitment to long-term employment in a regional community setting.

Why Join?
Rewarding work making a real difference in seniors’ lives, ongoing training and professional development, supportive team culture with regular staff recognition, modern country facilities with quality resources, and career growth potential within a respected not-for-profit organisation.

Please note: We are acting as recruitment agents on behalf of our client. Employer details will be provided to shortlisted candidates.

Vasse Pharmacy
Retail Pharmacist
Vasse Medical Centre
Shop 1/21 Napoleon Promenade
Vasse WA 6280, Australia
Full-Time | Permanent

$105 000  - $110 000 per year plus Super

Welcome to Vasse Pharmacy!
Vasse Pharmacy is a community-focused pharmacy committed to providing professional, patient-centred healthcare services, medication advice, and quality pharmacy support to the local community.
As our business continues to grow, we are seeking a qualified and experienced Retail Pharmacist to join our team. This position is pharmacy-focused, involving the dispensing of prescriptions, provision of professional healthcare advice, medication management, and support of day-to-day pharmacy operations.

About the Role
The Retail Pharmacist will be responsible for delivering high-quality pharmacy services, ensuring the safe and accurate dispensing of medications, providing professional advice to customers, and supporting the effective operation of the pharmacy.
The role will also involve working closely with pharmacy assistants, dispensary staff, healthcare professionals, and customers to ensure excellent service delivery and compliance with pharmacy standards and legislative requirements.

Key Responsibilities
• Dispense prescription medications accurately and in accordance with relevant legislation, pharmacy standards, and professional guidelines.
• Provide professional advice to customers regarding prescription medications, over-the-counter products, health conditions, and medication safety.
• Review prescriptions for accuracy, appropriateness, dosage, interactions, and patient suitability.
• Conduct medication counselling and support patients with medication adherence and understanding.
• Manage and maintain accurate dispensing records and pharmacy documentation.
• Support medication management services, including staged supply, dose administration aids, and medication reviews where applicable.
• Liaise with doctors, healthcare professionals, suppliers, and customers regarding medication-related enquiries and patient care.
• Supervise and support pharmacy assistants, dispensary technicians, and other pharmacy team members.
• Assist with stock control, ordering, inventory management, and ensuring appropriate storage of medications.
• Maintain compliance with workplace health and safety standards, pharmacy regulations, and company procedures.
• Support the delivery of professional services, health promotions, vaccinations, and community pharmacy initiatives where applicable.
• Ensure all work is completed with a strong focus on patient care, accuracy, confidentiality, and professional service.

Benefits and Perks
• Competitive salary package of $105 000 - $110 000 plus superannuation, depending on experience. 
• Long-term full-time opportunity within a supportive community pharmacy environment
• Opportunity to work closely with patients and make a meaningful contribution to the local community
• Supportive team environment with opportunities for professional development and growth

Qualifications and Experience
• Bachelor of Pharmacy or equivalent qualification
• Current registration as a Pharmacist with the Pharmacy Board of Australia / AHPRA or have provisional AHPRA registration in order to perform their duties under a licensed and fully registered pharmacist
• Minimum 2 years of relevant post-qualification experience in a similar environment, retail or community pharmacy
• Experience in prescription dispensing, patient counselling, and pharmacy operations
• Experience with pharmacy dispensing software is highly regarded
• Vaccination accreditation is desirable but not essential

Skills
• Strong knowledge of pharmacy practice, medication safety, and relevant legislative requirements
• Ability to dispense accurately and efficiently in a busy retail pharmacy environment
• Excellent communication and customer service skills
• Strong attention to detail and commitment to professional standards
• Ability to provide clear medication advice and patient counselling
• Strong organisational and time management skills
• Ability to work both independently and as part of a team
• Commitment to patient care, confidentiality, and ethical pharmacy practice
• Ability to supervise and support pharmacy team members
• Commitment to workplace health, safety, compliance, and continuous improvement

$105 000  - $110 000 per year plus Super

Full-time Cook position available with competitive salary. Work in a dynamic team in Byron Bay, 2979. 

3 Stand-out Bullet Points:

•	Full-Time Cook
•	Salary Range: $75,000 - $95,000 per annum plus superannuation
•	Exciting opportunity to work in a professional setting.

About Us
Sun Ranch is a premier hospitality and restaurant destination located in the heart of Byron Bay, NSW. We are committed to delivering exceptional culinary experiences, showcasing high-quality, locally sourced produce, and providing outstanding service in a vibrant and welcoming environment. Our kitchen operates at a fast pace, driven by a passionate team dedicated to culinary excellence and sustainable hospitality practices.

About the role
The Cook is responsible for preparing, cooking, and presenting high-quality food in accordance with the establishment's menus and standards. The role plays a critical part in ensuring the efficient operation of the kitchen, maintaining strict adherence to food safety and hygiene regulations, managing stock effectively, and supporting the broader culinary team to deliver an exceptional dining experience for our guests.

Duties and Responsibilities

•	Prepare, cook, and present menu items in accordance with standard recipes, portion controls, and presentation specifications.
•	Assist with the development and execution of daily specials and seasonal menu changes as directed by the Head Chef.
•	Ensure all food is prepared in a timely manner to meet service requirements and guest expectations.
•	Accommodate dietary requirements and allergy requests with strict adherence to cross-contamination protocols.
•	Maintain a high standard of cleanliness and sanitation throughout the kitchen, including workstations, equipment, and storage areas.
•	Strictly comply with the Australia New Zealand Food Standards Code and local food safety regulations.
•	Monitor and record food temperatures, cooling times, and storage conditions in accordance with the venue's Food Safety Program (HACCP).
•	Ensure all kitchen equipment is operated safely and maintained in good working order, reporting any defects or hazards immediately.
•	Receive and inspect food deliveries to ensure quality, correct quantities, and appropriate temperature controls.
•	Implement strict stock rotation procedures using the First In, First Out (FIFO) method.
•	Monitor inventory levels, conduct regular stocktakes, and assist with ordering supplies to prevent shortages.
•	Minimise food wastage through careful preparation, proper storage, and efficient use of ingredients.


Essential Skills

•	Strong technical cooking skills and a refined palate.
•	Ability to multitask, prioritise duties, and work efficiently under pressure during peak service periods.
•	Excellent interpersonal skills with the ability to work collaboratively and communicate effectively within a diverse kitchen brigade.
•	Precision in food preparation, plating, and adherence to recipes and safety protocols.
•	Capacity to adapt to changing menus, seasonal ingredients, and varying guest volumes.

Qualifications needed:

•	Minimum Certificate III trade qualification or equivalent relevant work experience
•	Minimum one year of work experience on relevant position

What We Offer

•	Competitive salary based on experience
•	Opportunities for professional growth and training
•	A supportive and dynamic work environment
•	Work on exciting projects with cutting-edge technology

Salary:  The role offers a remuneration package ranging from $75,000-$95,000 plus superannuation for a 38-hour work week.

How to Apply: 11 Recruitment is your pathway to securing this exciting opportunity. We are looking forward to facilitating your application and potentially welcoming you to a company that values expertise. Apply now and let us help you take the next step in your career.

result.description:
MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Transform lives, every single day

Do you want a career that means more? At Anglicare Sydney, we bring the strength, the support and the strategy to make it happen. 

For over 170 years, Anglicare has supported people and communities across Sydney and the surrounds. Our Seniors Communities portfolio spans Retirement Living and Support at Home services, supporting thousands of older Australians and their families. 

We'relooking for aCyberRisk andControls Analystto join our Cyber Security and IT Risk team. This role focuses onperforming risk assessmentsin accordancewiththe team's practises andguidelines as well as implementing andassessingcyber security controls,in alignment to the Cyber uplift program,supporting governance and compliance initiatives, and helping strengthen Anglicare's cyber security posture. Working closely with business and technology stakeholders, you will contribute to controls assurance activities, risk assessments and continuous monitoring programs that help protect Anglicare's critical systems,dataand digital assets.

As part of a purpose-driven organisation, you'll be working in a collaborative and values-led environment where your work directly contributes to enriching lives and strengthening communities. 

Your opportunity

TheCyber Risk and Controls Analystplaysan important rolein supporting Anglicare's cyber security governance, risk management,and to alesser degree,controlsimplementation andassuranceactivities. You willdeterminesecurityeffectivenessthrough risk assessments,aswell as implementing and assessing cyber security controls, in alignment to the Cyber uplift program,monitorcompliance with security frameworks and standards, and provide insights that help strengthen cyber resilience across the organisation.

Working alongside Cyber Security, ITArchitectureand business stakeholders, you will support control validation, governance frameworks, riskassessmentsand remediation initiatives while helping ensure Anglicaremaintainsa secure and resilient technology environment.

With ownership, you will:

You will support the development and maintenance of governance and compliance frameworks, conduct risk assessments and gap analyses,monitorcontrol performance and remediation activities, and contribute to security assurance initiatives. You will also prepare reports and documentation, support governanceprocessesand work closely with stakeholders to strengthen cyber security controls and reduce organisational risk.

What you'll bring

You are a cyber security professional with experience inrisk assessments,controls assurance,complianceandgovernance. You have agoodunderstanding of cyber security control frameworks,in particular the SCF framework,compliancerequirementsand security best practices, and enjoy analysing complex environments toidentifycontrol gaps and opportunities for improvement.

You combine strong analytical and problem-solving skills with excellent communication and stakeholder engagement capabilities. You are detail-oriented,collaborativeand proactive, with the ability to translate technical findings into practical recommendations that support business and securityobjectives. You are also committed to continuous learning and staying informed about emerging threats,technologiesand regulatory developments.

You will also need:

- Tertiary qualification in Information Technology, Cyber Security, RiskManagementor a related field. Certifications such as CRISC, CISM or ISO 27001 are highly desirable.
- 3+ years' experience in cyber security, governance, riskmanagementor compliance-related roles.
- Experience assessing andvalidatingcyber security controls and supporting controls assurance activities.
- Knowledge of cyber security frameworks and standards including SCF, NIST Cybersecurity Framework, NIST SP 800-53 and CIS Controls.
- Experience with control testing, evidence review, gap analysis and remediation tracking.
- Understanding of continuous control monitoring, compliancereportingand security assurance practices.
- Strong analytical, problem-solving and risk assessment capabilities.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to engage technical and non-technical stakeholders.
- Strong documentation and reporting skills with exceptional attention to detail.
- Proven ability to collaborate effectively across teams and contribute to organisation-wide cyber security and governance initiatives.

Why Anglicare?

At Anglicare, we provide meaningful opportunities and choice - both for the communities we support and the people who work with us. 

Here'swhatyou'llenjoy: 

Flexible work options to balance life and career. 

Salary packaging benefits - up to $15,900 of your income tax free, plus $2,650 for meals and entertainment. 

Ongoing professional development and career pathways. 

Exclusive staff discounts with over 400 retailers. 

Employee Assistance Program and Fitness Passport with access to 800+ gyms. 

Belonging to a supportive, purpose-driven team committed to making a difference. 

Apply now

Are you ready to help us attract and empower the people who will shape Anglicare's future? To apply, click the'Apply'button andsubmityour resum and cover letter. All applicants will receive a response. Anglicare is as wonderfully diverse as the communities we serve. While guided by our Christian values, our team includes people of all faiths and backgrounds.

We strongly encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, and people of all ages, genders,abilitiesand cultural backgrounds. 

Disclaimer:

We do not accept unsolicited agency resumes and are not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes.
